correctness.rationale: After unitary normalization the Fourier matrix is \(T_\zeta=((1,1),(1,\zeta))\). Its squared singular values are \(2\pm|1+\zeta|\), and evaluation at a difference of order \(m\) runs through all \(m\)-th roots of unity. Optimizing the cosine distance to \(-1\) gives the formulas for \(L(E)\), \(U(E)\), \(\rho(E)\), and \(D(E)\) exactly.
